title: Simple chemical reaction
competency: Define chemical reaction and give examples.

keywords.def: A process that changes substances into one or more new substances.
The starting materials in a chemical reaction.
The new substances formed in a chemical reaction.

en.text: In a chemical reaction the starting materials, the reactants, change into new substances, the products. We write Reactants → Products. The arrow means "produce". When magnesium burns, magnesium and oxygen are the reactants and magnesium oxide is the product: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.

screens.title: A broken beaker
screens.ask: A glass beaker falls and breaks. Is a new substance formed?
screens.after: Only the shape changed. No new substance formed, so it is a physical change, not a chemical reaction.

screens.title: 3.3.1 Simple chemical reaction
paras: The starting materials of a reaction are called reactants.
They react to produce one or more new substances, called products.
A chemical reaction changes reactants into products: Reactants → Products.

screens.title: Writing a reaction
paras: The arrow (→) is read as "produce", "give", "form" or "yield".
Reactants go on the left of the arrow. Products go on the right.
A "+" sign means "combines with" or "reacts with".

screens.title: Examples
paras: The reactants are magnesium and oxygen. The product is a white ash, magnesium oxide.
Iron + sulfur → iron sulfide. Iron sulfide is the product.
screens.note: Rusting of iron, fermentation and digestion of food are chemical reactions.

screens.text: In 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, what are the reactants?
screens.why: Reactants are on the left of the arrow.
screens.clue: Which side holds the starting materials?

screens.title: Chemical or physical?
screens.why: A chemical change forms a new substance.

screens.ask: In iron + sulfur → iron sulfide, the product is iron ___
screens.why: Iron sulfide is the new substance on the right.
screens.clue: What is on the right of the arrow?

screens.text: Cooking injera is a chemical change.
screens.why: Cooking forms new substances; it cannot be undone.
screens.clue: Can you turn baked injera back into batter?

screens.text: In a reaction, what does the arrow (→) tell you?
opts: The products turn back into reactants
screens.why: The arrow is read as "produce", "give", "form" or "yield".
